\subsection{Extension of the finite tensor certificate to five atoms}
\label{F:sec:r6-five-atom-errors}
The earlier Hardy mass-interpolation lemma already holds for any
number of positive atomic factors. For five atoms at degree nine,
the angular polynomial has four independent angle variables and
frequency indices between zero and nine in each variable. Put
$d_0=10$, $G=R=10^8$, and let $M_0$ be the integer coefficient
$\ell^1$ sum after multiplying and rounding the five single-atom
coefficient vectors. The exact polynomial and exponential
enclosures are unchanged. Sorting the masses at a vertex is
legitimate because the supremum over all support angles is
invariant under permutation of the factors.

For four angular contractions the scaled rounded root data have
complex error below $1/R$ relative to the corresponding exact
unit roots. Their accumulated error is therefore at most
\[
 ((1+1/R)^4-1)\frac{M_0}{G}
       <\frac{5M_0}{GR}.
\]
Each contraction has complex rounding error below one in integer
scale, including its binary64 arithmetic error as in the earlier
tensor proof. Its propagation through the remaining contractions
is at most
\[
 \sum_{j=0}^3\bigl(d_0(1+1/R)\bigr)^j<5d_0^3.
\]
Consequently the implementation's pads $5M_0/(GR)$ and
$5d_0^3/G$ cover the fourth angular variable as well as the
preceding three. The separate product-coefficient rounding pad
and five-factor input-vector enclosure are added exactly, as in
the original certificate.

For clarity, the forward-error allowance also extends to the
fourth binary64 contraction. Set $U=M_0+8d_0^4$. Before that
stage the sum of the absolute real and imaginary coordinates over
its remaining frequency index is at most
\[
 8M_0+8d_0^3+4d_0^2+2d_0<16U.
\]
This follows inductively because phase multiplication increases
the coordinate $\ell^1$ sum by at most two and every rounded
complex output contributes less than two to that coordinate sum.
The earlier three stages satisfy smaller bounds. With
$\gamma_{64}=64/(2^{53}-64)$, the same allowance
$\eta=16U\gamma_{64}$ bounds every real dot product, addition or
subtraction, and division by $R$: each dot has length ten and
$64>2\cdot10+6$. The implementation checks
\[
 20RU<2^{63},\qquad \eta<1/1000,
 \qquad 2(1/2+\eta)^2<1.
\]
They ensure exact representation of the input and rounded
intermediate integers in binary64 and complex rounding error
strictly below one per stage. Ordinary correctly rounded IEEE
binary64 arithmetic remains the computational assumption.

For an even angular grid size $L>18$, centered trigonometric
interpolation in the four angle variables divides the resulting
upper bound by
\[
 \left(1-\frac{9^2}{8}\left(\frac{22}{7L}\right)^2\right)^4>0.
\]
Only the first angle may use the conjugation half-grid; the other
three angles use their full grids. This covers every grid point
because complex conjugation reverses all angles simultaneously.
Two separately certified grid sizes may be tried adaptively; each
one gives a valid upper bound on the entire angular continuum.
The mass boxes use the sum of five Hardy interpolation remainders.
These arguments validate the finite method only. A whole mass-band
conclusion additionally requires a completed matching run with
an empty search stack and an actual exit-zero terminal certificate.

\section{Revised residual ledger after the twenty additional rounds}\label{col:F:34}
\label{F:sec:r6-ledger}
The 120 supplied main manuscripts were indexed and screened.  Only the
selected arguments rederived in the preceding sections are adopted as
proved conclusions.  The attached per-strand ledgers distinguish proof
review from statement screening; this revision does not certify every
claim in the supplied collection.  The baseline all-degree four-atom
exclusion remains in force.  The unrestricted conjecture is still not
proved.

\subsection{The ninth coefficient}
The new support-free upper mass cut is $t<13/4$ for every competitive
candidate.  Combining it with the exact ground-state witnesses and the
inherited defect-one lower bound gives the following ledger.  Endpoints
are excluded, so the indicated residual mass intervals are open.
\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{ccc}
\toprule
Support $N$ & Previously retained mass interval & Revised status\\
\midrule
$5$&$[\frac{9}{5},9/2)$&Entire stratum excluded\\
$6$&$[\frac{3}{2},9/2)$&$\frac{178547}{100000}<t<13/4$\\
$7$&$[\frac{9}{7},9/2)$&$\frac{14413}{10000}<t<13/4$\\
$8$&$(\frac{34}{27},9/2)$&$\frac{34}{27}<t<13/4$\\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
The old mass intervals in this table describe the earlier scalar
projection, not a claim that every point in those intervals survived
all old tests.  Neither interval length nor a list of necessary filters
measures the volume of the residual configuration space.

Within every retained stratum, the following new necessary conditions
must hold simultaneously for the same positive Herglotz measure and
its matching spectral data:
\begin{enumerate}
\item All finite ground-state matrices $E+tV-(9/N)M$ are positive
semidefinite, and the physical Gram and derivative inequalities of
Section~\ref{F:sec:r6geometry} hold.
\item $|M_1|>t/1400$; equivalently the product of all Cayley zero
radii after removing one designated zero at the origin, with
multiplicity, is greater than $1/1400$. An additional zero at the
origin makes this product zero. This uses the four-row certificate
and supersedes the earlier conservative $1/27000$ consequence.
\item Every interior auxiliary spectral root $w$ obeys
$9\log(1/|w|)-\Re H(w)<1/2$ and $\Re H(w)>11/8$.
\item The calibrated sign set has harmonic measure greater than $1/4$
and its negative-half cosine-square integral is at least $7/36$.
\item If the maximum scaled auxiliary depth $A=9\max_j\ell_j$
is at most $2$, the projected coefficient spread of
Section~\ref{F:sec:r6projectedenergy} must satisfy $D_2>3/40$.
\item The projected three-grid tube of halfwidth $1/36$ and the
bijectively matched nine-grid tube of halfwidth $(9-N)/13500$ are
absent.  At $N=8$, every eight-point subset of a rotated regular decagon
is absent even without an auxiliary phase condition.
\end{enumerate}
For completeness, support sizes $N\le3$ at degree nine are excluded
directly by the new comparison: $t\ge(3(9/N)-1)/2\ge4>13/4$,
contradicting the support-free ninth-row theorem. Support size four
is covered by the complete four-atom theorem retained in this paper.

These tests strengthen the existing full stationary moment equations,
first-third and cyclic coefficient inequalities; they do not replace
any of them.  Cayley zeros, interior auxiliary roots, and reciprocal
outer factors retain their distinct definitions.
There are now three unclosed deficient support-size strata at degree
nine: $N=6,7,8$.  This is a count of support types, not a count of boxes.
The full-support equality family remains admissible at $N=9$.
No finite ninth-degree residual box catalogue analogous to the earlier
384-box eighth-degree catalogue is claimed by this revision.

\subsection{All degrees}
The ground-state hierarchy, sixth-index coefficient gap theorem and its
stable low-energy version, projected-energy radial exclusions,
all-depth grid exclusions, and calibrated
sign restrictions apply to arbitrary degrees with their stated
hypotheses.  They close explicitly defined infinite families.
They do not force an arbitrary deficient candidate into an excluded
family.  The complete all-degree four-support theorem is preserved;
no new complete all-degree support-size stratum above four is claimed.
The support-density and sparse-ray envelopes from the first revision
remain valid, with all new tests imposed inside them.

\section{The updated remaining mathematical obligation}\label{col:F:35}
\label{F:sec:residual-scope}
\subsection{A support-size envelope after the four-atom closure}
\label{F:sec:post-four-residual}

Theorem~\ref{F:thm:all-four-support} removes the entire deficient
four-support stratum, with no upper restriction on the coefficient
index.  A one-atom deficient candidate is also impossible: the
necessary mass bound gives $t\ge n$, and
Theorem~\ref{F:thm:uniform-n-tail} gives a strict coefficient bound.
Together with the supplied complete two- and three-support exclusions,
any competitive deficient candidate that remains in this research
programme must therefore have $N\ge5$.

The following inherited table records necessary index envelopes; additional finite holes from Section~\ref{F:sec:r6-ledger} are imposed inside them.  The lower
end uses the known sixth- and seventh-coefficient theorems
and their equality classifications \cite{F:wik,F:xie}, together with
the deficient condition $n>N$.  The upper end uses the inherited
sparse-support rays, with the improved nine-support ray proved here.
An entry does not assert that every pair in that interval is genuinely
open or that a stationary candidate exists there: all other
compatibility conditions and regional exclusions still apply.
\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{ccc}
\toprule
Support size $N$&Necessary coefficient-index envelope&Excluded ray\\
\midrule
$5$&$8\le n\le36,\ n\ne9$&$n\ge37$\\
$6$&$8\le n\le45$&$n\ge46$\\
$7$&$8\le n\le54$&$n\ge55$\\
$8$&$9\le n\le63$&$n\ge64$\\
$9$&$10\le n\le72$&$n\ge73$\\
$10$&$11\le n\le82$&$n\ge83$\\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
For every $N\ge11$, the general density bound proved in this paper
also gives the exact necessary envelope
\[
 N+1\le n<\frac{500000}{52279}\,N,
 \qquad\text{equivalently}\qquad
 n\le\left\lceil\frac{500000N}{52279}\right\rceil-1.
\]
Thus each fixed support size has only finitely many possible indices,
but the support size itself is unbounded.  This is still an infinite
family of continuous constrained problems, rather than a new finite
catalogue replacing the earlier 384-box computation.


Let $\mathcal R_{n,N}$ denote the competitive stationary candidates
that satisfy the complete reduction, including positivity of the
original measure, the shared support, coefficient compatibility,
all stationary moment equations, the spectral identities and all
previously proved exclusions.  This notation is not a definition
using scalar bounds alone.  In a convenient auxiliary-root
convention the common-support moment equations include
\[
 \sum_{j=1}^{N}(r\lambda_j-1)\alpha_j^r
 =\frac12\sum_{\ell=1}^{d}
    \left(\sigma_\ell^r+\overline{\sigma_\ell}^{-r}\right),
 \qquad 1\le r\le n,
 \quad 0<|\sigma_\ell|<1.
\]
They must hold for the same support points, masses and auxiliary
roots at every index.  Independently satisfying their separate
absolute-value envelopes is not enough.

The new necessary restrictions include, for every candidate,
\[
 E_{\mathrm{third}}:=2\sum_{j=1}^{\lfloor n/3\rfloor}|M_j|
 >\min\left\{\frac{d^2}{2nN},\frac1{12}\right\}.
\]
At $t\ge3/2$ this strengthens to $E_{\mathrm{third}}>1/12$,
and at $t\ge2$ to $E_{\mathrm{third}}>1/10$.
If $n=3k$, then the off-lattice quantity
\[
 E_{\mathrm{cyclic}}:=
 2\sum_{\substack{1\le j\le n\\k\nmid j}}|M_j|
\]
must exceed $3(t-1)/5\ge3d/(5N)$ at $t<3/2$, and must exceed
$1/3$ at $t\ge3/2$.  The finite residue majorant provides a stronger
test than this total-size condition whenever the locations of the
nonzero moments restrict the number of products that can reach the
target degree.

The new phase conditions, completed finite rows and downward
support-free upper slabs are also imposed simultaneously.
The last certificate ledger specifies exactly which finite support
strata have been closed in this continuation.  It never promotes
a partial run or a sampled phase configuration to a completed row.

To complete the support-exclusion route to the unrestricted proof,
it remains to establish
\[
 \boxed{\qquad
 \mathcal R_{n,N}=\varnothing
 \quad\text{for every relevant } n
 \text{ and every }1\le N<n.\qquad}
\]
We have not proved this assertion.  This route also forces the
expected equality classification; the weak sharp coefficient bound
alone could in principle be proved without strictly excluding
deficient equality cases.  In particular, no theorem here
forces all surviving candidates to have a sufficiently small
first-third moment sum or cyclic error.  Large values of those sums
are not contradictions; they define part of the remaining domain.
Nor do the finite computations supply an all-degree cutoff for all
support sizes.

One equivalent coefficient-side target makes the remaining obstacle
especially explicit.  In the stationary reflected factorization,
put
\[
 X(z)=\prod_{j=1}^{N}(1-\alpha_jz)
       \prod_{\ell=1}^{d}(1-\sigma_\ell z),\qquad
 p=\prod_{\ell=1}^{d}|\sigma_\ell|.
\]
With the usual positive phase normalization, the exact spectral
identity from the supplied first-round radial paper is
\[
 a_n=e^{-t}p^{-1}\|X\|_{H^2}^2.
\]
Here is the normalization directly.  Normalize $a_0=e^{-t}>0$
and $a_n>0$, and form the stationary reflected polynomial
\[
 R(z)=\sum_{j=0}^{n}a_jz^j+
                  \sum_{j=0}^{n-1}\overline{a_j}z^{2n-j}.
\]
Its physical support roots are $\zeta_j=\overline{\alpha_j}$,
each double.  If its interior auxiliary roots are $s_\ell$,
choose $\sigma_\ell=\overline{s_\ell}$; the paired exterior roots
are $1/\overline{s_\ell}$.  This is exactly the auxiliary convention
in the moment equations above.  The factorization with its fixed
constant term is
\[
 R(z)=e^{-t}\prod_j(1-\alpha_jz)^2
       \prod_\ell(1-\sigma_\ell z)
                         (1-\overline{\sigma_\ell}^{-1}z).
\]
On the unit circle it gives
\[
 z^{-n}R(z)=e^{-t}\frac{\kappa}{p}|X(z)|^2,
 \qquad
 \kappa=(-1)^n\prod_j\alpha_j
                     \prod_\ell\frac{\sigma_\ell}{|\sigma_\ell|}.
\]
The unit factor $\kappa$ equals $1$ because the stationary density
$z^{-n}R$ is nonnegative and is not identically zero.
Taking its circle mean, which is the middle coefficient $a_n$,
proves the asserted identity.  In particular, the parameters
$\sigma_\ell$ lie inside the disk, while the zeros of the factors
$1-\sigma_\ell z$ in $X$ lie outside it; these two conventions
are distinct.
Therefore the desired sharp coefficient bound on these candidates
is precisely
\begin{equation}\label{F:eq:global-gap-target}
 t\ge1+\log\frac{\|X\|_{H^2}^2}{2p}.
\end{equation}
This is a reformulation of the sharp coefficient bound, not an additional
proved inequality. Excluding all competitive deficient candidates,
which are defined using $a_n\ge2/e$, requires the strict version of
\eqref{F:eq:global-gap-target}, or a separate equality classification
forcing the full-support configuration. The known unit-circle entropy theorem treats
the full-degree reduction; it does not establish
\eqref{F:eq:global-gap-target} for arbitrary deficient factors with
interior auxiliary roots.  None of the new arguments fills that
remaining gap.  This identifies where a genuinely global next
step is needed, rather than declaring the finite catalogue or a
list of research questions to be the last proof.

\subsection{Why support recurrence alone does not force the new small-error tests}
\label{F:sec:relaxation-obstruction}

The direct moment estimates cannot be turned into a global cover merely
by adding positivity, a common finite support, its exact linear moment
recurrence, the mass bounds and the necessary slope bound
$\Phi\ge n/2$.  The following explicit family demonstrates this
limitation.  It is a counterexample to that relaxed implication, not
a candidate satisfying the full stationary equations and not a
counterexample to the coefficient conjecture.

\begin{proposition}[Common support does not imply a small moment error]
For every $n\ge5$ there is a positive measure on $N=n-1$ distinct
points with $\lambda_j\ge1/n$, $n/N\le t<n$ and $\Phi\ge n/2$,
whose moments satisfy the exact support recurrence at every index,
but whose first-third error exceeds $1$.  If $n=3k\ge6$, its
cyclic off-lattice error exceeds $5$.  None of these measures
satisfies the full one-defect stationary moment equations.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
Fix $n\ge5$, put $N=n-1$, and take all $N$th roots of unity
$\alpha_j=e^{2\pi i j/N}$, $0\le j<N$.  Set
\[
 \eta=\frac12,\qquad t=\frac{2n}{N},\qquad
 \lambda_j=\frac{t}{N}(1+\eta\Re\alpha_j).
\]
These are positive masses on exactly $N$ distinct points, and
\[
 \sum_j\lambda_j=t,\qquad
 \lambda_j\ge\frac{t(1-\eta)}N=\frac{n}{N^2}\ge\frac1n,
 \qquad \frac nN\le t<n.
\]
Discrete Fourier orthogonality gives the entire moment sequence
explicitly:
\[
 M_r=t\left\{\mathbf1_{N\mid r}
       +\frac\eta2\mathbf1_{N\mid r-1}
       +\frac\eta2\mathbf1_{N\mid r+1}\right\}.
\]
Thus every moment comes from the same positive measure, and the
exact support recurrence $M_{r+N}=M_r$ holds at all indices.
All its Toeplitz moment matrices are positive semidefinite; their
rank is $N$ once the matrix size is at least $N$, because the
weights are positive and the support points are distinct.

The slope bound also holds.  Write $\alpha_j=e^{-i\theta_j}$;
the reflected root set is the same regular polygon.  The cotangent
partial-fraction identity, differentiated once, gives
\[
 \sum_{j=0}^{N-1}\csc^2\frac{\theta-\theta_j}{2}
     =N^2\csc^2\frac{N\theta}{2}.
\]
Consequently, away from the poles,
\[
 \Phi(\theta)
 =\frac12\sum_j\lambda_j\csc^2\frac{\theta-\theta_j}{2}
 \ge\frac n2\csc^2\frac{N\theta}{2}\ge\frac n2.
\]

Nevertheless, $m=\lfloor n/3\rfloor\le N-2$, so the only
nonzero moment among $M_1,\ldots,M_m$ is $M_1=t\eta/2$.
The first-third error is therefore
\[
 2\sum_{r=1}^{m}|M_r|=t\eta=\frac t2>1,
\]
far outside either small-error slab proved in this continuation.
If $n=3k\ge6$, neither $1$ nor $N=n-1$ is divisible by $k$;
both indices occur in the cyclic error sum.  Hence
\[
 2\sum_{\substack{1\le r\le n\\k\nmid r}}|M_r|
 \ge 2(|M_1|+|M_N|)=t\eta+2t=\frac{5t}{2}>5.
\]
No inequality forcing the required smallness of these errors can
follow solely from the relaxed properties just verified.

The failure of full stationarity is explicit and quantitative.
Here $d=n-N=1$.  At $r=2$, Fourier orthogonality gives both
$M_2=0$ and $\sum_j\alpha_j^2=0$, so
\[
 \sum_j(2\lambda_j-1)\alpha_j^2=0.
\]
For a single admissible auxiliary root $\sigma=\rho e^{i\vartheta}$,
$0<\rho<1$, the required right side of the stationary equation
has modulus
\[
 \left|\frac{\sigma^2+\overline\sigma^{-2}}2\right|
 =\frac{\rho^2+\rho^{-2}}2>1.
\]
Thus this equation has a residual exceeding one in modulus on the
whole displayed family.
\end{proof}

The example is not part of the fully compatible stationary residual.
It locates the missing logical step: a global argument must exploit the simultaneous stationary
moment and coefficient identities, beyond the common-support
recurrence and the scalar or pointwise necessary bounds.

\section{The precise correction in the deficient entropy route}\label{col:F:36}
\label{F:sec:entropy-obstruction}

The unit-circle entropy theorem of Lei--Zhang, in the programme of
Agler--McCarthy \cite{F:agler,F:lei}, does not apply directly to the
deficient spectral factor.  The obstruction can be stated as exact
identities and explicit examples.  These statements identify a failed
extension of a proof method; they are not counterexamples to the
Krzy\.{z} conjecture.

\subsection{An exact entropy identity with auxiliary roots}

Use the conventions of Section~\ref{F:sec:residual-scope}.  Write
\[
 X(z)=\prod_{j=1}^{N}(1-\alpha_jz)
       \prod_{\ell=1}^{d}(1-\sigma_\ell z)
       =\sum_{j=0}^{n}x_jz^j,
 \qquad S=\|X\|_2^2,\qquad p=\prod_\ell|\sigma_\ell|.
\]
Define
\[
 b_r=\int_{\mathbb T}|X(z)|^2z^r\,dm(z)
     =\sum_{j=0}^{n-r}x_j\overline{x_{j+r}},
 \qquad
 c_r=\frac1r\sum_{\ell=1}^{d}
             (\sigma_\ell^r-\overline{\sigma_\ell}^{-r}),
 \quad 1\le r\le n.
\]
The entropy of the normalized density is
\[
 \mathcal E(X)=\frac1S\int_{\mathbb T}|X|^2\log|X|^2\,dm-\log S.
\]

\begin{proposition}[Deficient entropy correction]
\label{F:prop:deficient-entropy-identity}
For a positive stationary tuple satisfying the complete common-support
log-jet identities, one has
\[
 tS=\int_{\mathbb T}|X|^2\log|X|^2\,dm
                       +\operatorname{Re}\sum_{r=1}^{n}c_rb_r.
\]
Consequently its positively normalized coefficient obeys
\begin{equation}\label{F:eq:deficient-entropy-identity}
 -\log a_n=\mathcal E(X)+\mathcal D(X),\qquad
 \mathcal D(X)=\log p+\frac1S\operatorname{Re}
                                      \sum_{r=1}^{n}c_rb_r.
\end{equation}
In particular, the desired weak bound is equivalent to
$\mathcal E(X)+\mathcal D(X)\ge1-\log2$ on the full stationary
set.  Excluding competitive deficient tuples requires strictness
or a separate equality classification.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
Let $M_r=\sum_j\lambda_j\alpha_j^r$ and
$g(z)=t+2\sum_{r\ge1}M_rz^r$, so that $f=e^{-g}$.
The analytic logarithm of $X$, with constant term zero, has coefficients
\[
 q_r=-\frac1r\left(\sum_j\alpha_j^r+
                              \sum_\ell\sigma_\ell^r\right).
\]
The given stationary moment equations say exactly
$-2M_r=2q_r+c_r$ for $1\le r\le n$.
The polynomial $X$ vanishes at each physical support point
$\overline{\alpha_j}$.  Therefore the finite Fourier identity gives
\[
 0=\sum_j\lambda_j|X(\overline{\alpha_j})|^2
   =tS+2\operatorname{Re}\sum_{r=1}^{n}M_rb_r.
\]
On the other hand,
\[
 \int_{\mathbb T}|X|^2\log|X|^2\,dm
     =2\operatorname{Re}\sum_{r=1}^{n}q_rb_r.
\]
This follows by radial approximation of the logarithms of the unit-root
factors; their boundary logarithms are integrable, and $|X|^2$ is a
trigonometric polynomial of degree $n$.  The outer factors have analytic
logarithms on a neighborhood of the closed disk.  Substitution proves the
first identity.  Finally $a_n=e^{-t}S/p$ gives
$-\log a_n=t+\log p-\log S$, proving
\eqref{F:eq:deficient-entropy-identity}.
\end{proof}

When $d=0$, the correction vanishes and all the zeros of $X$ lie on
the unit circle.  The established entropy inequality then supplies
the required estimate.  When $d>0$, neither the same entropy bound
for $X$ nor a favorable sign for $\mathcal D(X)$ follows merely
from the location of its zeros.

\subsection{A mixed-root counterexample to the automatic extension}

\begin{proposition}[Failure arbitrarily close to the unit-root boundary]
\label{F:prop:mixed-root-entropy-failure}
For $0<r<1$, put
\[
 X_r(z)=(1-iz)(1+irz)=1-i(1-r)z+rz^2.
\]
It has one unit-circle zero, one zero outside the disk, constant
coefficient $1$, and positive leading coefficient $r$.  Nevertheless
\[
                  \mathcal E(X_r)<1-\log2\qquad(0<r<1).
\]
Its spectral phase is the positive one: if
\[
 R_r(z)=(1-iz)^2(1+irz)(1+ir^{-1}z),
\]
then $z^{-2}R_r(z)=r^{-1}|X_r(z)|^2\ge0$ on $\mathbb T$.
At $r=1/2$, the putative correction also has the wrong sign:
\[
 S=\frac32,\qquad
 \mathcal E(X_{1/2})=\frac7{12}-\log\frac32,
 \qquad
 \mathcal D(X_{1/2})=\frac38-\log2<0.
\]
Here $\mathcal D$ denotes the same algebraic expression in
\eqref{F:eq:deficient-entropy-identity}; the example is not a stationary
positive-measure tuple.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
Only the first two logarithmic Fourier coefficients are needed.  Direct
calculation gives
\[
 S(r)=2(1-r+r^2),\qquad
 A(r):=\int|X_r|^2\log|X_r|^2\,dm
               =2-5r+6r^2-r^3.
\]
Thus $\mathcal E(X_r)=A(r)/S(r)-\log S(r)$ and
\[
 \frac{d}{dr}\mathcal E(X_r)
   =\frac{-2(r-1)(r+1)(r^2+2r-1)}{S(r)^2}.
\]
The derivative is negative on $(0,\sqrt2-1)$ and positive on
$(\sqrt2-1,1)$.  Both endpoint limits are $1-\log2$, proving the
strict inequality throughout the open interval, including parameters
arbitrarily close to $1$.

For $r=1/2$, $A=7/8$.  With $\sigma=-i/2$, the correlations and
logarithmic correction coefficients are
\[
 b_1=\frac i4,\quad b_2=\frac12,
 \qquad c_1=\frac{3i}{2},\quad c_2=\frac{15}{8}.
\]
Their real pairing is $9/16$, giving $\mathcal D=3/8-\log2$.
The elementary inequalities $\log2>1/2$ and
$\log(4/3)<1/3$ certify both strict failures without numerical
quadrature.  The displayed identity for $R_r$ follows directly
from the paired-root factorization.

To check the scope, the first stationary equation for
$\alpha=i$ and $\sigma=-ir$ would require
\[
 \lambda-1=-\frac{r+r^{-1}}2,
 \qquad\text{hence}\qquad
 \lambda=1-\frac{r+r^{-1}}2<0.
\]
This contradicts positivity.  Thus the example refutes the relaxed
entropy and correction claims, while explicitly failing a required
stationary premise.
\end{proof}

The polar-factor step also fails for this relaxed class.  At $r=1/2$,
let $q=X-(zX')/2=1-iz/4$.  The same two-coefficient computation gives
\[
 \int|X|^2\log|q|^2\,dm=\frac5{32},\qquad
 \int|X|^2\log|X/q|^2\,dm=\frac{23}{32}<\frac32=\|X\|_2^2.
\]
Thus the sharp polar lower bound for unit-root polynomials cannot be
carried over unchanged.  In particular, reflection relative to degree
two gives $q+q^*=1+z^2$, which is different from $X$ when $r<1$.

\subsection{The direction of radial motion and its admissibility}

\begin{proposition}[Exact outward radial monotonicity]
\label{F:prop:radial-norm-direction}
Fix all factors except one and write $X_r=(1-r\omega z)Y$, where
$|\omega|=1$, $Y\ne0$, and $p=rp_0$.  Put
$A=\|Y\|_2^2$ and $C=\operatorname{Re}\langle\omega zY,Y\rangle$.
Then
\[
 \frac{\|X_r\|_2^2}{rp_0}
       =\frac{A(r+r^{-1})-2C}{p_0},\qquad
 \frac{d}{dr}\frac{\|X_r\|_2^2}{rp_0}
       =\frac A{p_0}(1-r^{-2})<0\quad(0<r<1).
\]
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
Multiplication by $z$ is an isometry in $H^2$, so
$\|X_r\|_2^2=A(1+r^2)-2rC$.  Division and differentiation prove
both formulas.
\end{proof}

Consequently moving auxiliary radii outward decreases the right side
of the desired mass inequality
$t\ge1+\log(\|X\|_2^2/(2p))$ when $t$ is fixed.  A bound proved
only at the unit-root endpoint does not imply the stronger interior
bound.  Allowing the mass to vary requires an admissible variation
that satisfies all the shared moment identities; radial motion alone
does not provide one.

This last obstruction occurs even at genuine positive stationary
tuples.  For every $k\ge1$, take $n=2k$, $N=k$, equal masses $t/k$
on $\alpha_j^k=1$, and auxiliary parameters satisfying $\sigma_\ell^k=r$.
The complete nonzero log-jet equations are exactly
\[
 t-1=\frac{r+r^{-1}}2,\qquad
 2t-1=\frac{r^2+r^{-2}}2.
\]
All other indices through $2k$ vanish by the root-of-unity sums.
Writing $u=r+r^{-1}>2$, the two equations force
\[
 u^2-2u-4=0,\qquad
 t=\tau:=\frac{3+\sqrt5}{2},\qquad
 r=\tau-1-\sqrt{(\tau-1)^2-1}.
\]
The function $f(z)=\exp[-\tau(1+z^k)/(1-z^k)]$ realizes this
tuple.  Its reflected polynomial factors as
\[
 e^{-\tau}(1-z^k)^2(1-rz^k)(1-r^{-1}z^k),
\]
so the spectral density is nonnegative.  These are the exact
stationary audit functions already identified in Revision~4
\cite{F:source}; their coefficients lie strictly below the competitive
threshold.  Indeed, writing $\phi=\tau-1$, one has
$\phi^2=\phi+1$, $\phi<2$, and
\[
 e^\phi>1+\phi+\frac{\phi^2}{2}+\frac{\phi^3}{6}
       =2\phi+1+\frac{4-\phi}{6}>2\phi+1.
\]
Since $a_{2k}=(4\tau-2)e^{-\tau}$, this proves $a_{2k}<2/e$.
Within this radial family there is no nonconstant stationary path:
the equations force the single displayed value of $r$ and $t$.
Equivalently, differentiating them gives
\[
 \frac{(1-r)(1+r^3)}{r^3}\,r'=0,
\]
so $r'=0$ while $0<r<1$.  The calculation does not rule out a
different global variational argument.  It does rule out treating
the proposed radial interpolation as automatically stationary.

The remaining entropy obligation is therefore the inequality in
Proposition~\ref{F:prop:deficient-entropy-identity} on the full positive,
common-support stationary set.  Neither the mixed-root entropy bound,
the sign of the correction, nor a stationary path to the unit-root
boundary has been established for that set by this argument.

\section{Reproduction and source identity}\label{col:F:37}
The revised payload contains both the byte-preserved baseline certificate
files and the selected new material under \texttt{revision2/}. The source
texts and checking data of the first ten supplied rounds are additionally
preserved under \path{revision2/prior_source/}, including the originals
behind the inherited two- and three-support claims. Their inclusion is
provenance, not a declaration that every historical claim has been
independently rechecked in this revision.
The new \texttt{--revision} mode runs only this revision's 10 exact
arithmetic checkers; \texttt{--quick} includes them with the baseline
quick checks. Source manuscripts preserved for provenance are not
blanket-certified by their inclusion. All newly developed mathematical
arguments are printed in the body. An optional finite five-atom full replay is
included in this build. Use \texttt{--ninth-five} to replay only the
completed degree-nine five-atom continuum certificate, or \texttt{--full}
to include it after all inherited finite certificates. The quick modes
do not rerun this longer continuum search; they retain its checked
source identity and completed record in the hash-verified payload.

The single source file generates a reproduction program using
\texttt{filecontents*}.  The same program is embedded as an attachment
in this PDF.  It contains the checking programs, rational parameters,
the reproduced upper-mass witnesses, completed output logs, and exact
command records used in this continuation.  It verifies the hashes
of its packaged files before extraction.  No external download of
the supplied tournament is needed to replay those included checks.

Use \texttt{python reproduce\_\allowbreak krzyz\_\allowbreak followup.py --extract DIR}
to reconstruct the files in a fresh directory.  Its
\texttt{--quick} option runs the new analytic arithmetic checks;
\texttt{--high} additionally replays the inherited support-free Laurent
witnesses and the four-support phase sources;
\texttt{--full} additionally replays the new direct degree-five through
degree-seven bases, the inherited degree-eight through degree-ten
four-support certificates and the selected completed finite
rows in the final ledger. Python, NumPy and SymPy are needed;
the inherited integer Fourier checker also requires a C++17 compiler.
The full finite replay can take substantially longer than the
analytic checks.  Running a source with Python's \texttt{-O} option
would disable assertions and is not a valid verification.

The scope of each conclusion is determined by its theorem and the
complete continuous cover proved for its verifier.  Neither the
number of arithmetic checks nor a successful source compilation
is a substitute for that reasoning.

\part{Cumulative scope and reproduction}
\label{part:synthesis}
\section{The cumulative remaining domain}
\label{col:current}
The complete all-degree deficient four-support exclusion is retained
from Theorem~\ref{F:thm:all-four-support}. The five-support completion
at degree nine is Section~\ref{F:sec:r6-n9-five-atom-join}. These are
different quantified statements: the former holds for every $n>4$
with $N=4$; the latter concerns exactly $(n,N)=(9,5)$.

\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{cp{0.36\linewidth}p{0.35\linewidth}}
\toprule
Degree-nine support & Cumulative status & Necessary residual mass range\\
\midrule
$N\le4$ & Excluded from competitive candidates & None\\
$N=5$ & Entire stationary stratum excluded & None\\
$N=6$ & Not yet excluded completely & $178547/100000<t<13/4$\\
$N=7$ & Not yet excluded completely & $14413/10000<t<13/4$\\
$N=8$ & Not yet excluded completely & $34/27<t<13/4$\\
$N=9$ & Full-support theorem and equality case & Canonical equality retained\\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
Every retained candidate must additionally satisfy the same-measure
conditions in Section~\ref{F:sec:r6-ledger}. In particular,
$|M_1|>t/1400$, every internal auxiliary root $w$ obeys
$9\log(1/|w|)-\Re H(w)<1/2$ and $\Re H(w)>11/8$, and the
projected-energy, signed-size, Gram, and geometric exclusions apply
with their stated joint hypotheses. The intervals in the table are
necessary scalar projections. They are not assertions that a stationary
candidate exists at every mass in an interval.

The three remaining support sizes do not determine a number of open
boxes. In the completed five-atom computation, 2,114 accepted terminal
boxes certify coverage of a domain that has already been excluded.
The 951 mass knots in the high-mass certificate, the 376 knots in the
four-row certificate, and the earlier 384-box eighth-degree catalogue
are also different indexing devices. They must not be added or
subtracted as though they counted the same residual objects.

For general degree, the current necessary support-density condition is
$N/n>52279/500000$, together with the sharper fixed-support rays and
all regional restrictions proved in the text. The earlier bound
$N/n>873/10000$ remains a valid weaker consequence and is retained
with its original argument. The stronger density threshold alone does
not close an unbounded range of support sizes.

The remaining global obligation is still
\[
 \mathcal R_{n,N}=\varnothing
 \qquad\text{for every relevant integer }n\text{ and }1\le N<n,
\]
where $\mathcal R_{n,N}$ retains the full stationary compatibility
system. For the ninth coefficient this reduces to the three sets
$\mathcal R_{9,6}$, $\mathcal R_{9,7}$ and $\mathcal R_{9,8}$.
Their emptiness has not been proved in this collection.

\section{Coverage, revisions, and the preserved research record}
\label{col:coverage}
This edition contains all twenty-five main sections of the initial
general-degree fourth revision and all thirty-seven main sections of
the completed continuation. Their eighteen and two appendices,
respectively, follow the common bibliography. The latest initial
revision retains all seventy cross-reference labels from the
second revision and all 139 labels from the third revision. The original
second- and third-revision TeX sources are preserved in the combined
reproduction payload for inspection.

The three initial cycle records contain exactly sixty questions:
ten cycles with G1--G6 in each cycle. They are printed in
Appendix~\ref{P:sec:r4-ledger}. The thirty initial embedded source and
checking files are preserved without changing their bytes. The
continuation reproduction program is also preserved byte for byte;
its own payload contains 773 hash-identified files, including accepted
proof sources, exact witnesses, completed records, and source
manuscripts kept for provenance. The presence of an unadopted source
manuscript does not certify every claim in that manuscript.

The following distinctions govern the collection:
\begin{itemize}
\item A theorem is stated with the hypotheses used in its proof;
a numerical or symbolic checker verifies its specified finite inputs.
\item A historical completion record identifies a previously finished
execution. Its preservation is not a claim that this compilation
repeated that entire computation.
\item A failed proposed implication is retained as an obstruction;
an auxiliary counterexample is not relabelled as a counterexample
to the Krzy\.{z} conjecture.
\item The full-support entropy theorem is proved inside the text.
The deficient case retains its correction term, and its global
inequality is still an obligation.
\end{itemize}
The new editorial material organizes the discussion and reconciles its
scope. It does not claim a new support-size completion beyond the
accepted theorems retained from the completed continuation.

\section{Reproducing the collected edition}
\label{col:reproduction}
The single TeX file compiles without another manuscript file. It writes
the original thirty initial support files, the original continuation
program, and the combined program
\path{reproduce_krzyz_collected.py} into the build directory. The PDF
embeds the combined program, so the entire checking material can also
be recovered directly from its attachment.

The combined program contains its sources and data in a hash-checked
archive. Extraction additionally invokes the original continuation
extractor, which verifies every one of its 773 file hashes:
\begin{lstlisting}[language=bash]
python reproduce_krzyz_collected.py --extract recovered
\end{lstlisting}
The target directory must be empty. The original foundation files are
under \path{recovered/foundation/}, the unchanged continuation program
is under \path{recovered/followup/}, and its expanded checking tree is
under \path{recovered/followup/certificates/}. Original source texts,
coverage records and manifests are included alongside them.

The available modes have deliberately different scopes:
\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{p{0.22\linewidth}p{0.68\linewidth}}
\toprule
Mode & Work performed\\\midrule
\texttt{--quick} & Twelve shorter initial symbolic/rational audits,
followed by the continuation's complete quick mode.\\
\texttt{--foundation} & The twelve initial audits, the improved
all-degree tail certificate with its finite bases, and the independent
moment/gap reconstruction in the required order.\\
\texttt{--revision} & The ten exact-arithmetic checkers from the last
continuation revision.\\
\texttt{--ninth-five} & The completed five-atom, degree-nine continuum
search only; this is a longer replay.\\
\texttt{--full} & The complete foundation replay followed by all
finite and high-mass replays supplied by the continuation.\\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
Run Python with assertions enabled. The last-revision exact mode uses
the Python standard library. Some inherited quick checks require
SymPy. Complete finite replays also require NumPy and a C++17 compiler
for the supplied Fourier checker. The binary64 tensor certificates use
the explicit forward-error assumptions and pads proved in the text;
they are not described as all-rational computations.

Original reproduction instructions in the preserved sections remain
valid after compiling this single source. In particular, the initial
independent tail reconstruction consumes the JSON report created by
the preceding tail verifier; the combined program preserves that
dependency. A quick replay does not stand in for the longer continuum
search or an all-degree covering theorem.

\section{The complete adaptive ten-cycle ledger}
\label{P:sec:r4-ledger}
\begingroup\emergencystretch=2em
The six research-question labels used in this ledger are:
G1, exact common-support constraints; G2, moment and boundary
consequences; G3, cardinal and conditioned Gram structure;
G4, diffuse geometry and covering tests; G5, the competitive
coefficient and variational tests; G6, adversarial audit and scope.
These are working streams, not replacements for the original problem
or its success criteria.  The target coefficient bound and equality
problem have not been weakened.  No claim of a complete global proof,
formal proof-assistant verification, or historical priority is made.
The record below contains ten iterations of each stream, sixty
questions in total.  A status of ``retained'' denotes a useful identity
or conditional test, not an additional excluded region.  A status of
``failed'' denotes a proposal for which the stated goal was not proved,
or an explicitly disproved shortcut.  Shared findings are credited
within the records; the three paired streams were asynchronous.

\subsection{Cycle 1}

\paragraph{G1. Can the first n weighted moments retain their common support through one annihilating polynomial?}
\emph{Attempt.} Set B(\allowbreak{}x)\allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{}prod(\allowbreak{}x-\allowbreak{}alpha\_j)\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} M\_k=\allowbreak{}sum lambda\_j alpha\_j\textasciicircum{}k. Multiply B(\allowbreak{}alpha\_j)\allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{}0 by lambda\_j alpha\_j\textasciicircum{}k and sum.

\emph{Outcome (retained).} Derived sum b\_l M\_(\allowbreak{}k+\allowbreak{}l)\allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{}0. For d=\allowbreak{}1 the k=\allowbreak{}0 and k=\allowbreak{}1 equations use only the known moments; both are retained exactly.

\emph{Next question.} Use the Chebyshev recurrence without replacing support moments by independent boxes.

\paragraph{G2. Do those two annihilator equations force a regular support polygon?}
\emph{Attempt.} Substitute M\_k=\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}p\_k+\allowbreak{}T\_k(\allowbreak{}q)\allowbreak{}z\textasciicircum{}k)\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}k into the annihilator,\allowbreak{} retaining the unknown coefficients b\_l and total mass t.

\emph{Outcome (failed).} No such implication was obtained: the coefficients still encode the unknown support and the equations are necessary identities. They are not counted as a new exclusion.

\emph{Next question.} Try a recurrence-\allowbreak{}based positive constraint whose sign does not require knowing B.

\paragraph{G3. Can a light-\allowbreak{}cardinal lower bound retain an arbitrary light polynomial P?}
\emph{Attempt.} Factor Q=\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}z-\allowbreak{}a)\allowbreak{}CP; write V=\allowbreak{}P/\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}z-\allowbreak{}beta)\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} (\allowbreak{}z-\allowbreak{}a)\allowbreak{}V=\allowbreak{}P+\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}beta-\allowbreak{}a)\allowbreak{}V,\allowbreak{} and use coefficient Cauchy-\allowbreak{}Schwarz.

\emph{Outcome (proved).} Proved lambda\_beta >\allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} (\allowbreak{}L/\allowbreak{}sqrt(\allowbreak{}ell)\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}delta*\allowbreak{}|\allowbreak{}|\allowbreak{}V|\allowbreak{}|\allowbreak{})\allowbreak{}\textasciicircum{}2/\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}delta\textasciicircum{}2*\allowbreak{}|\allowbreak{}Pprime(\allowbreak{}beta)\allowbreak{}|\allowbreak{}\textasciicircum{}2)\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} when |\allowbreak{}|\allowbreak{}CP|\allowbreak{}|\allowbreak{}>\allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{}L|\allowbreak{}|\allowbreak{}C|\allowbreak{}|\allowbreak{} and the bracket is positive.

\emph{Next question.} Find light polynomials with a uniform multiplication lower bound L.

\paragraph{G4. Can low coefficient autocorrelations certify such a bound for irregular supports?}
\emph{Attempt.} Write the multiplication Gram matrix and apply Hermitian Gershgorin to its Toeplitz diagonals.

\emph{Outcome (retained).} Retained explicit L\textasciicircum{}2 >\allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} |\allowbreak{}|\allowbreak{}P|\allowbreak{}|\allowbreak{}\textasciicircum{}2-\allowbreak{}2 sum\_\{k=\allowbreak{}1\}\textasciicircum{}\{ell-\allowbreak{}1\}|\allowbreak{}corr\_k(\allowbreak{}P)\allowbreak{}|\allowbreak{} when positive; no universal small-\allowbreak{}correlation premise is justified.

\emph{Next question.} Test whether the cardinal framework alone could force an unrestricted contradiction.

\paragraph{G5. Can a mass Hessian add a new sign condition to the stationary moment equations?}
\emph{Attempt.} Differentiate the coefficient under lambda\_j+\allowbreak{}s c\_j; derive the exact second derivative Re[z\textasciicircum{}n]f H\_c\textasciicircum{}2.

\emph{Outcome (retained).} Obtained a finite coefficient formula for every real mass direction; its relation to the already-\allowbreak{}imposed stationary polynomial was unresolved.

\emph{Next question.} Compare this derivative with R0=\allowbreak{}f+\allowbreak{}O(\allowbreak{}z\textasciicircum{}(\allowbreak{}n+\allowbreak{}1)\allowbreak{})\allowbreak{}.

\paragraph{G6. Does differentiating Re(\allowbreak{}a\_n)\allowbreak{} preserve the actual extremal target?}
\emph{Attempt.} Normalize a\_n>\allowbreak{}0 and use the fact that every coefficient maximizer also maximizes Re(\allowbreak{}a\_n)\allowbreak{} after phase rotation.

\emph{Outcome (audit).} The real-\allowbreak{}part second-\allowbreak{}variation condition is necessary,\allowbreak{} but strict local maximality would still not imply the global competitive level.

\emph{Next question.} Test independence before adding Hessian positivity as a new exclusion.

\subsection{Cycle 2}

\paragraph{G1. What does the Chebyshev recurrence imply directly for the atoms?}
\emph{Attempt.} Expand S\_(\allowbreak{}k+\allowbreak{}2)\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}2qz S\_(\allowbreak{}k+\allowbreak{}1)\allowbreak{}+\allowbreak{}z\textasciicircum{}2 S\_k using S\_k=\allowbreak{}sum(\allowbreak{}k lambda\_j-\allowbreak{}1)\allowbreak{}alpha\_j\textasciicircum{}k.

\emph{Outcome (retained).} Obtained the exact confluent atomic recurrence recorded in the proof fragment for k=\allowbreak{}1,\allowbreak{}...,\allowbreak{}n-\allowbreak{}2.

\emph{Next question.} Audit the k=\allowbreak{}0 equation before using this as an elimination system.

\paragraph{G2. Can the same atomic recurrence be imposed with zero right-\allowbreak{}hand side at k=\allowbreak{}0?}
\emph{Attempt.} Compare the auxiliary value S\_0=\allowbreak{}1 with the atomic expression S\_0=\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}N,\allowbreak{} where N=\allowbreak{}n-\allowbreak{}1.

\emph{Outcome (audit).} No. The atomic expression has right-\allowbreak{}hand side -\allowbreak{}n z\textasciicircum{}2. Dropping this correction would add a false constraint; the exact auditor checks it.

\emph{Next question.} Seek a positive Gram condition that is independent of this indefinite moment recurrence.

\paragraph{G3. Do cardinal identities,\allowbreak{} the scalar mass strip,\allowbreak{} and the spectral coefficient ratio alone force a contradiction?}
\emph{Attempt.} Constructed exact Q=\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}z-\allowbreak{}2/\allowbreak{}3)\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}z\textasciicircum{}4-\allowbreak{}1)\allowbreak{} at n=\allowbreak{}5 and computed all four cardinal norms.

\emph{Outcome (failed).} The proposed shortcut fails: masses (\allowbreak{}1,\allowbreak{}11/\allowbreak{}50,\allowbreak{}1/\allowbreak{}4,\allowbreak{}1/\allowbreak{}4)\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} t=\allowbreak{}43/\allowbreak{}25,\allowbreak{} satisfy the cardinal identities,\allowbreak{} simple mass strip,\allowbreak{} and the algebraic ratio competitiveness test.

\subsection{First-third coefficient checks}
\begin{lstlisting}[language=Python]
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Exact checks accompanying the all-degree first-third proof.

The proof, not this finite test suite, establishes the all-degree assertion.
Checks cover the unbounded-ray polynomial certificate, exponential rational
comparisons, finite-jet factorization, and dependent complex frame examples.
"""
from fractions import Fraction as Q
from math import factorial
from pathlib import Path
import json
import sympy as s

checks = []


def check(name, condition):
    if not bool(condition):
        raise AssertionError(name)
    checks.append(name)


def exp_prefix(v, n):
    out = [s.Integer(1)] + [s.Integer(0)] * n
    for k in range(1, n + 1):
        out[k] = s.expand(sum(j * v[j] * out[k-j]
                             for j in range(1, k+1)) / k)
    return out


check("exp(9/10) > 49/20 by degree-five sum",
      sum(Q(9,10)**k / factorial(k) for k in range(6)) - Q(49,20)
      == Q(35033,4000000))
check("exp(5/12) > 3/2 by degree-three sum",
      sum(Q(5,12)**k / factorial(k) for k in range(4)) - Q(3,2)
      == Q(161,10368))
y, u = s.symbols("y u", real=True)
P = s.Rational(1,4) - s.Rational(13,20)*y + s.Rational(9,40)*y**2 + s.Rational(49,120)*y**3
expm = s.Rational(49,20)*(1+y+y**2/2+y**3/6)
check("ray polynomial expansion", s.expand(expm-(y+2)*(y+s.Rational(11,10))-P) == 0)
Pu = s.expand(P.subs(y,u+s.Rational(1,2)))
quad = s.Rational(19,30)*u**2-s.Rational(19,160)*u+s.Rational(31,960)
check("ray lower quadratic remainder", s.expand(Pu-quad-s.Rational(49,120)*u**2*(u+s.Rational(1,2))) == 0)
check("positive completed-square margin",
      Q(31,960)-Q(19,160)**2/(4*Q(19,30)) == Q(821,30720))
check("monotone second branch at t=3/2", -Q(3,2)**2+Q(29,10)*Q(3,2)-Q(9,10) == Q(6,5))
check("monotone second branch at t=2", -4+Q(29,10)*2-Q(9,10) == Q(9,10))
t = s.symbols("t", positive=True)
check("entropy derivative identity", s.simplify(s.diff(t-1-s.log(t)-(t-1)**2/(2*t),t)-(t-1)**2/(2*t**2)) == 0)

# Exact positive symmetric atomic measures give real rational moments while
# their Hilbert vectors are genuinely complex. Some middle frames are dependent.
roots = [s.Integer(1), s.Integer(-1), s.Rational(3,5)+s.Rational(4,5)*s.I,
         s.Rational(3,5)-s.Rational(4,5)*s.I]
weights = [s.Rational(1,5),s.Rational(1,10),s.Rational(7,20),s.Rational(7,20)]
D = s.diag(*weights)
one = s.ones(4,1)

for n, mass in [(2,s.Rational(1,2)), (5,s.Integer(1)),
                (8,s.Rational(3,2)), (11,s.Integer(3)),
                (17,s.Integer(5))]:
    m=n//3+1
    powers = [s.Matrix([s.expand(z**j) for z in roots]) for j in range(n+1)]
    rho=[s.simplify((one.conjugate().T*D*v)[0]) for v in powers]
    check(f"real rational positive-measure moments n={n}", all(r.is_Rational for r in rho))
    eps=2*mass*sum(abs(rho[j]) for j in range(1,m))
    mom=[mass*r for r in rho]
    full=[s.Integer(0)]+[-2*mom[j] for j in range(1,n+1)]
    low=[s.Integer(0)]+[full[j] if j<m else s.Integer(0) for j in range(1,n+1)]
    high=[s.Integer(0)]+[full[j] if j>=m else s.Integer(0) for j in range(1,n+1)]
    fjet=exp_prefix(full,n)
    ljet=exp_prefix(low,n)
    gjet=[(s.Integer(1) if k==0 else high[k])+
          sum(high[j]*high[k-j] for j in range(k+1))/2 for k in range(n+1)]
    check(f"quadratic truncation and low convolution n={n}",
          all(s.simplify(sum(ljet[j]*gjet[k-j] for j in range(k+1))-fjet[k])==0
              for k in range(n+1)))
    for k in range(2*m,n+1):
        V=s.Matrix.hstack(*powers[m:k-m+1])
        _, pivots=V.rref()
        B=V[:,list(pivots)]
        G=B.conjugate().T*D*B
        Proj=B*G.inv()*B.conjugate().T*D
        p=s.simplify(Proj*one)
        q=s.simplify(Proj*powers[k])
        H=s.simplify((p.conjugate().T*D*p)[0])
        Hq=s.simplify((q.conjugate().T*D*q)[0])
        C=s.simplify((p.conjugate().T*D*q)[0])
        S=sum(rho[j]*rho[k-j] for j in range(m,k-m+1))
        F=V*V.conjugate().T*D
        check(f"equal projection norm n={n} k={k}", H==Hq and 0<=H<=1)
        check(f"frame cross term n={n} k={k}", s.simplify((p.conjugate().T*D*F*q)[0]-S)==0)
        check(f"projection residual Cauchy n={n} k={k}", abs(rho[k]-C)<=1-H and abs(C)<=H)
        check(f"frame perturbation n={n} k={k}", abs(S-C)<=eps*H/mass)
        check(f"quadratic moment bound n={n} k={k}",
              abs(mom[k]-sum(mom[j]*mom[k-j] for j in range(m,k-m+1)))
              <=mass*max(1,abs(mass-1)+eps))
        if len(pivots)<V.cols:
            check(f"dependent frame explicitly covered n={n} k={k}", V.rank()==len(pivots))

report={"status":"PASS","checks":len(checks),"scope":"Exact finite checks supporting the displayed all-degree analytic proof; not an exhaustive residual enumeration.","names":checks}
out=Path(__file__).with_name("third_band_verification.json")
out.write_text(json.dumps(report,indent=2)+"\n")
print(json.dumps({"status":report["status"],"checks":len(checks),"report":str(out)},indent=2))
\end{lstlisting}

\subsection{Cubic core interval certificates}
\begin{lstlisting}[language=Python]
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Exact arithmetic certificates for the cubic cyclic-core exclusion.

The continuum arguments are in cubic_resonance.tex.  This script checks
the finite rational inequalities in its proof, not sampled functions.
"""
from fractions import Fraction as Q
from math import factorial
import json
from pathlib import Path


def exp_lower(x, order=40):
    x = Q(x)
    assert x >= 0
    term = Q(1)
    out = term
    for j in range(1, order + 1):
        term *= x / j
        out += term
    return out


def exp_upper(x, order=40):
    x = Q(x)
    assert 0 <= x < order + 2
    first = x ** (order + 1) / factorial(order + 1)
    return exp_lower(x, order) + first / (1 - x / (order + 2))


checks = []


def check(name, assertion):
    assert assertion, name
    checks.append(name)


def A(t):
    return 1 - 2 * t + Q(2, 3) * t * t


cap = Q(67, 100)
check("first analytic maximum: 3 exp(-3/2) < 67/100",
      Q(9) < cap * cap * exp_lower(Q(3)))
check("second analytic maximum: 2 sqrt(6) exp(-2) < 67/100",
      Q(24) < cap * cap * exp_lower(Q(4)))
check("decreasing tail at t=9/2", Q(99, 2) < cap * exp_lower(Q(9, 2)))

slabs = []
for numerator in range(280, 540):
    lo, hi = Q(numerator, 120), Q(numerator + 1, 120)
    abs_a = max(abs(A(lo)), abs(A(hi)))
    b = 2 * hi - 1
    c = b - abs_a
    check(f"positive cubic denominator on slab {numerator}", c > 0)
    core_square = max(Q(1), 4 * b ** 3 / (27 * c))
    margin = cap * cap * exp_lower(2 * lo) - 4 * lo * lo * core_square
    check(f"entire rational mass slab {numerator}/120..{numerator+1}/120", margin > 0)
    slabs.append({"lower":str(lo), "upper":str(hi), "A_upper":str(abs_a),
                  "B_upper":str(b), "C":str(c), "squared_margin":str(margin)})

check("exp(1/3) < 67/48", exp_upper(Q(1,3)) < Q(67,48))
check("exp(3/10) < 27/20", exp_upper(Q(3,10)) < Q(27,20))
check("e < 30/11", exp_upper(Q(1)) < Q(30,11))
check("high-mass final coefficient margin", cap + Q(1,16) == Q(293,400))
check("293/400 < 11/15", Q(293,400) < Q(11,15))
check("low-mass quadratic margin", Q(11,45)-Q(243,1000) == Q(13,9000))

# Exact symbolic identities are verified as polynomial coefficient arrays.
import sympy as sp
t, a, y, s = sp.symbols("t a y s", real=True)
aa = sp.symbols("A", real=True, nonnegative=True)
expression = aa*a**3 + (1-a**2)*(1+2*s*a*y-(1-a)*y**2)
inner = 1+(s**2-1)*a**2+(s**2+aa)*a**3
outer = (1+2*s)*a+(aa-1-2*s)*a**3
check("Schur quadratic vertex", sp.factor(expression.subs(y,s*a/(1-a))-inner) == 0)
check("Schur quadratic endpoint", sp.factor(expression.subs(y,1)-outer) == 0)
check("switch agreement", sp.factor((inner-outer).subs(a,1/(1+s))) == 0)
At = 1-2*t+sp.Rational(2,3)*t**2
check("negative-A denominator", sp.expand((2*t-1)+At-sp.Rational(2,3)*t**2)==0)
check("tail monotonicity polynomial", sp.expand(sp.diff(2*t*At,t)-2*t*At-(-sp.Rational(4,3)*t**3+8*t**2-10*t+2))==0)
check("tail endpoint derivative", (-sp.Rational(4,3)*t**3+8*t**2-10*t+2).subs(t,sp.Rational(9,2)) == -sp.Rational(5,2))

# Test the third coefficient identity by a formal exponential calculation.
m1,m2,m3=sp.symbols("m1 m2 m3")
z=sp.symbols("z")
third=sp.series(sp.exp(-2*(m1*z+m2*z**2+m3*z**3)),z,0,4).removeO().coeff(z,3)
check("third coefficient identity", sp.expand(third-(-2*m3+4*m1*m2-sp.Rational(4,3)*m1**3))==0)

# Off-lattice first-order cancellation is an integer divisibility identity.
for k in range(1,13):
    for m in range(1,9):
        n=m*k
        check(f"linear residue cancellation k={k},m={m}",
              all((n-j)%k!=0 for j in range(1,n+1) if j%k))

report={"status":"PASS", "exact_checks":len(checks), "rational_mass_slabs":len(slabs),
        "analytical_scope":"all t >= 3/2; the 260 slabs cover [7/3,9/2], with analytic initial interval and infinite tail",
        "checks":checks,"slabs":slabs}
path=Path(__file__).with_name("cubic_resonance_verification.json")
path.write_text(json.dumps(report,indent=2)+"\n")
print(json.dumps({k:report[k] for k in ("status","exact_checks","rational_mass_slabs","analytical_scope")},indent=2))

\subsection{Residue and finite-degree checks}
\begin{lstlisting}[language=Python]
"""Exact checks supporting the arithmetic transfer, not a substitute for its proof."""
from fractions import Fraction as Q
from math import factorial, gcd
import json
from pathlib import Path

checks = []

def check(name, condition):
    assert condition, name
    checks.append(name)

def exponential_jet(beta, n):
    out = [Q(1)] + [Q(0)] * n
    for r in range(1, n+1):
        out[r] = sum(j * beta.get(j, Q(0)) * out[r-j]
                     for j in range(1, r+1)) / r
    return out

def multiply(a, b, n):
    return [sum(a[j]*b[r-j] for j in range(r+1)) for r in range(n+1)]

# Independently expand the powers for a nontrivial multi-residue polynomial.
n = 18
beta = {1: Q(1,9), 4: Q(2,7), 7: Q(1,11), 13: Q(1,5)}
b = exponential_jet(beta, n)
base = [beta.get(j,Q(0)) for j in range(n+1)]
power = [Q(1)] + [Q(0)]*n
series = power[:]
for q in range(1,n+1):
    power = multiply(power, base, n)
    series = [v + w/factorial(q) for v,w in zip(series,power)]
check('finite recurrence equals independent power expansion', b == series)

# Boundary arithmetic: one residue, order exactly ten.
jet = exponential_jet({1:Q(3)},30)
check('single residue target projection',
      sum(jet[10*r] for r in range(1,4)) ==
      sum(Q(3**(10*r),factorial(10*r)) for r in range(1,4)))
check('single residue order', 10//gcd(1,10)==10)
check('uniform cancellation-order envelope',
      Q(67,100)+Q(11*3**10,8*factorial(10)) < Q(7,10))
e_upper = sum(Q(1,factorial(j)) for j in range(21)) + Q(2,factorial(21))
check('seven tenths strictly below target', Q(7,10)*e_upper < 2)

# The finite degree cutoff is strictly stronger than the infinite residue filter.
jet = exponential_jet({10:Q(7),13:Q(5),16:Q(9)},18)
check('arbitrary high-band noise contributes exactly zero',
      sum(jet[3*r] for r in range(1,7)) == 0)

# Real roots-of-unity filtering at k=2, including all finite terms.
jet = exponential_jet({1:Q(1,3)},12)
check('parity filter equals even factorial series',
      sum(jet[2*r] for r in range(1,7)) ==
      sum(Q(1,3**(2*r)*factorial(2*r)) for r in range(1,7)))

result = {'status':'PASS','checks':checks,'count':len(checks),
          'scope':'Exact finite-series and rational endpoint checks; uniform theorem proved analytically.'}
Path(__file__).with_suffix('.json').write_text(json.dumps(result,indent=2))
print(json.dumps(result,indent=2))

\subsection{The four-atom phase strip}
\begin{lstlisting}[language=Python]
"""Exact rational continuum certificate for n=26,N=4,46/5 <= t <= 93/10.

No floating point value is used in the acceptance path. The analytic
inequalities and continuum coverage are proved in spectral_phase_strip.tex.
"""
from fractions import Fraction as F
from pathlib import Path
from math import factorial,isqrt
import json

HERE=Path(__file__).resolve().parent
n,N=26,4
def atan_bounds(x):
    # 24 terms end with a negative term; 25 end with a positive term.
    lo=sum(((-1)**j*x**(2*j+1)/F(2*j+1) for j in range(24)),F())
    return lo,lo+x**49/F(49)
la,ua=atan_bounds(F(1,5));lb,ub=atan_bounds(F(1,239))
pl=F(3141592653589793,10**15);pu=F(3141592653589794,10**15)
assert pl<16*la-4*ub<16*ua-4*lb<pu
ehi=sum((F(1,factorial(j)) for j in range(20)),F())+F(21,20*factorial(20))
target=F(14715,20000)
assert target<2/ehi
def sqrt_bounds(x):
    S=10**15
    q=isqrt(x.numerator*S*S//x.denominator)
    lo,hi=F(q,S),F(q+1,S)
    assert lo*lo<=x<hi*hi
    return lo,hi
def trig_point(x,parity):
    assert 0<=x<2
    lo=sum(((-1)**j*x**(2*j+parity)/F(factorial(2*j+parity)) for j in range(12)),F())
    return lo,lo+x**(24+parity)/F(factorial(24+parity))
def sin_i(a,b):
    assert 0<=a<=b<pl/2
    return trig_point(a,1)[0],trig_point(b,1)[1]
def cos_i(a,b):
    assert 0<=a<=b<pl/2
    return trig_point(b,0)[0],trig_point(a,0)[1]
def tan_i(a,b):
    sl,su=sin_i(a,b);cl,cu=cos_i(a,b)
    return sl/cu,su/cl
def sec2_i(a,b):
    cl,cu=cos_i(a,b)
    return 1/cu**2,1/cl**2
rows=json.loads((HERE/'phase_strip_parameters.json').read_text())
assert len(rows)==40 and [r['j'] for r in rows]==list(range(40))
results=[]
for row in rows:
    j=row['j'];lo=F(46,5)+F(j,400);hi=F(46,5)+F(j+1,400)
    k,b,u=map(F,(row['k'],row['b'],row['u']))
    ps=list(map(F,row['p']))
    assert F(3,2)<=k<=F(5,2) and 0<u<F(1,2) and 0<b<=1
    assert len(ps)==3 and all(0<p<1 for p in ps)
    R=F(N,n)/pl
    z=(1-b)/(1+b)
    L=max(F(),F(1,2)-(2*atan_bounds(z)[1]+N*hi/n*b)/pl)
    a=1-lo/(2*n)
    al=1+sqrt_bounds(hi/n)[1]/(2*n*a)
    v=sqrt_bounds(k-lo/(2*n))[0]
    assert v*v>=a
    g=sqrt_bounds(F(2))[0]/al*(v+a/v-2*sqrt_bounds(a)[1])
    al_lo=1+sqrt_bounds(hi/n)[0]/(2*n*a)
    v_hi=sqrt_bounds(k-lo/(2*n))[1]
    g_hi=sqrt_bounds(F(2))[1]/al_lo*(v_hi+a/v-2*sqrt_bounds(a)[0])
    assert 0<g<=g_hi<1
    cp=lo/n-F(1,n*n)
    assert cp>0
    Fs=[k*sin_i(pl*u,pu*u)[1]/pl]
    for s,p in zip(range(2,5),ps):
        ymax=pu*u/(s-1)
        assert k*cos_i(ymax,ymax)[0]-cp*sec2_i(ymax/2,ymax/2)[1]>0
        x=(pl*u*p,pu*u*p);y=(pl*u*(1-p)/(s-1),pu*u*(1-p)/(s-1))
        sx=sin_i(*x);sy=sin_i(*y)
        cx=cos_i(*x);cy=cos_i(*y)
        tx=tan_i(x[0]/2,x[1]/2);ty=tan_i(y[0]/2,y[1]/2)
        ex=sec2_i(x[0]/2,x[1]/2);ey=sec2_i(y[0]/2,y[1]/2)
        beta=F(s-1,n*n)
        numerator=k*sx[1]+(s-1)*(k*sy[1]-2*cp*ty[0])-2*beta*tx[0]
        assert numerator>0
        Dl=k*cx[0]-beta*ex[1]-k*cy[1]+cp*ey[0]
        Du=k*cx[1]-beta*ex[0]-k*cy[0]+cp*ey[1]
        Fu=numerator/pl+u*max(F(),-p*Dl,(1-p)*Du)
        Fs.append(Fu)
    score=2*R/(k-1)+max(min(1-u,1-u-L+R),max(Fs)+(1-g)*R)
    assert score<target
    recorded_upper=F((score*10**12).__ceil__(),10**12)
    recorded_margin=F(((target-score)*10**12).__floor__(),10**12)
    assert score<=recorded_upper<target and 0<recorded_margin<=target-score
    results.append({'j':j,'lower_mass':str(lo),'upper_mass':str(hi),'upper_bound':str(recorded_upper),'margin_to_target':str(recorded_margin)})
summary={'status':'PASS','rational_mass_cells':40,'component_cases_per_cell':4,'coefficient_upper_target':str(target),'competitive_threshold_lower_bound':str(2/ehi),'n':n,'N':N,'covered_mass_interval':['46/5','93/10'],'strictly_new_interval':['46/5','93/10'],'new_interval_left_open':True,'claims_global_conjecture':False}
(HERE/'verification.json').write_text(json.dumps({'summary':summary,'cells':results},indent=2)+'\n')
print(json.dumps(summary,indent=2))
\end{lstlisting}
